mainTopic: The sources for lashes together with payment, and for lashes on a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and how רבי מאיר and the רבנן use the warning פסוקים for עדים זוממין
overview: The משנה had a מחלוקת. רבי מאיר says certain עדים זוממין get both מלקות and payment, while the רבנן say a person gets only one punishment, based on "כדי רשעתו". עולא says רבי מאיר learns it from מוציא שם רע, who is lashed and also pays. The comparison works because רבי מאיר agrees with רבי עקיבא that the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס. Some place עולא's teaching elsewhere instead: on רבי יהודה's view that a לאו שאין בו מעשה can bring lashes. The גמרא rejects each single source, first מוציא שם רע and then עדים זוממין. It then builds a הצד השוה from both cases and defends it against two attacks: that both involve a קנס, and that each has a צד חמור. Finally the גמרא returns to רבי מאיר and the רבנן and asks how each side uses the פסוקים "לא תענה" and "והנשארים ישמעו". That last answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Rabbis have a source, but what is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the חכמים's source for 'only one punishment' and asks for רבי מאיר's source for two punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense for the רבנן. The פסוק says 'according to his wickedness': you punish a person for one wrongdoing, not for two. But what is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the חכמים's view from a פסוק. Then it asks what source רבי מאיר could have for giving both lashes and payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "כדי רשעתו" (singular: 'his wickedness') teach that one act gets one punishment, so the חכמים say whoever pays is not lashed. רבי מאיר seems to go against this פסוק. So the גמרא wants to know what source lets him give two punishments for one act.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for this side; now what about the other?)
'According to his wickedness' (דברים 25:2)
One wrongdoing, which gets one punishment
What is the reason / source?

steps.confusionAlert: "רשעה" here does not mean the person is extra wicked. The point is that one sinful act gets one punishment, not two.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Granted, according to the Rabbis,
"according to his wickedness" is written,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2, the פסוק about giving lashes.

phrases.english: for one wrongdoing you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable for two wrongdoings.
But Rabbi Meir, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's מחלוקת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's ruling that one act can bring both lashes and payment

steps.title: עולא: רבי מאיר learns from the defamer
steps.stepSummary: עולא says רבי מאיר learns from מוציא שם רע, who is both lashed and pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: He learns it from the one who defames his wife. Just as the defamer is lashed and pays, so too anyone like him is lashed and pays.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives רבי מאיר's source. The Torah gives the מוציא שם רע both lashes and a payment, so the same can apply elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוציא שם רע shows that the Torah sometimes gives two punishments for one act. רבי מאיר takes this case and applies it as a general rule ('אף כל') to other cases, like עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it (from another case)
One who falsely defames his new wife
Gets lashes and also pays
So too everyone (the rule spreads to all similar cases)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
He learns it from the one who defames.
phrases.notes: This is a husband who falsely says his bride was not a בתולה; see דברים 22:18–19.

phrases.aramaic: מָה מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע – לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם,
phrases.english: Just as the defamer is lashed and pays,
so too anyone is lashed and pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: גָּמַר מִמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns from מוציא שם רע, who gets both lashes and payment

steps.title: But the defamer's payment is a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that מוציא שם רע is different, because his payment is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the defamer? He is special, because his payment is a fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's comparison. It says מוציא שם רע has a special feature that עדים זוממין may not share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a fixed amount set by the Torah, not payment for real damage. Maybe the Torah allows lashes together with a קנס, but not together with ordinary repayment. If so, you cannot learn עדים זוממין from מוציא שם רע.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X? It is special, because... (a way to break a comparison)
A fine: a fixed amount set by the Torah, not payment for actual loss

phrases.english: What about the defamer?
He is special, since his payment is a fine!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, שֶׁכֵּן קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of עדים זוממין to מוציא שם רע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מוציא שם רע pays a קנס, so the comparison does not prove anything about cases with ordinary payment

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds that the witnesses' payment is also a fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר agrees with רבי עקיבא that עדים זוממין's payment is a קנס, so the comparison works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי עקיבא, who says: the payment of conspiring witnesses is a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. For רבי מאיר, עדים זוממין also pay a קנס, just like מוציא שם רע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference raised in step 3 disappears once both payments count as a קנס. So רבי מאיר can learn from מוציא שם רע that lashes and payment go together.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (another תנא's opinion)
Witnesses proven false, who get the punishment they plotted for the other person

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, the source is מוציא שם רע. This works only because he agrees with רבי עקיבא that עדים זוממין pay a קנס.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who says: conspiring witnesses — it is a fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוציא שם רע's קנס makes it different from עדים זוממין
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, following רבי עקיבא, both payments are a קנס, so the comparison holds

steps.title: Second version: רבי יהודה on leftover קרבן פסח meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says some place עולא's teaching on a ברייתא where רבי יהודה rules there are no lashes for leaving over the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach עולא's statement on this ברייתא: 'Do not leave any of it until morning, and what is left until morning [burn in fire].' The verse puts a positive command after a prohibition, to teach that one is not lashed for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of where עולא's teaching belongs. It first quotes a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the Torah followed the prohibition with a command to burn the leftovers. This positive command fixes the sin, so there are no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (it differently)
Do not leave over (the קרבן פסח meat)
A positive command that comes after a prohibition and fixes it
One is not lashed for it

phrases.english: There are those who teach this statement of Ulla
on that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"You shall not leave any of it until morning,
and what is left of it until morning, etc." —
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: burn it in fire.

phrases.english: the verse comes to place a positive command
after a prohibition,
to say that one is not lashed for it;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּעוּלָּא אַהָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of where עולא's statement belongs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: no lashes for leaving over the קרבן פסח, because a positive command follows the prohibition

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: no lashes because no action is done
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the reason is different: this is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, which never brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: That is not the reason. Rather, it is because this is a prohibition with no action, and for any prohibition with no action one is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא agrees there are no lashes but gives a different reason. Leaving meat over is a sin done by doing nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the key point is that no action was done, not the burning command. Lashes need a sin done through an action. So any לאו שאין בו מעשה does not bring lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not for that reason
A prohibition broken without doing any action

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה agree on the result: no lashes here. They argue only about the reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
This is not for that reason;
rather, it is because it is
a prohibition with no action,
and any prohibition with no action,
one is not lashed for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for any לאו שאין בו מעשה

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה get lashes for a no-action prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא it follows that רבי יהודה holds a לאו שאין בו מעשה does bring lashes. The גמרא asks for his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: By inference, רבי יהודה holds that for a prohibition with no action one is lashed. From where does he know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא and asks for רבי יהודה's source. This sets up the next move, where עולא's teaching comes in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה needed a special reason (the positive command) to cancel lashes. That shows he thinks a לאו שאין בו מעשה would normally bring lashes. The גמרא now wants his source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference / it follows that
From where does he know it?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the spot where, in the second version, עולא's derivation from מוציא שם רע will be placed.

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Yehuda holds

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: that for a prohibition with no action one is lashed;
from where does he know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא and asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings lashes

steps.title: עולא: learned from the defamer
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that רבי יהודה learns his rule from מוציא שם רע, who gets lashes even though his sin is only speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: He learns it from the defamer. Just as the defamer breaks a prohibition with no action and is flogged, so too anyone who breaks a prohibition with no action is flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question from step 7: רבי יהודה learns his rule from the case of מוציא שם רע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוציא שם רע sins only with his mouth, so his sin is a לאו שאין בו מעשה. The Torah still gives him lashes. עולא makes this case the model for every לאו שאין בו מעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it, he derives it (from another case)
A husband who falsely accuses his new wife of unfaithfulness
A prohibition broken without any physical action
One gets lashes for it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא: גָּמַר מִמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע.
phrases.english: Ulla said: He derives it from the defamer.
phrases.notes: "He" means רבי יהודה, whose source the גמרא was looking for in step 7.

phrases.english: Just as the defamer

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: is a prohibition with no action, and one is flogged for it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: so too, for any prohibition with no action, one is flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: גָּמַר מִמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 about רבי יהודה's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns it from מוציא שם רע, a speech-only sin that brings lashes.

steps.title: The defamer is a stricter case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the source: מוציא שם רע is special because he is both flogged and pays money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the defamer? He is special, because he is flogged and also pays!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's source by showing that מוציא שם רע is a stricter case than ordinary prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn a rule from a case that is not unusually strict. מוציא שם רע gets two punishments for one sin, lashes and money. Maybe the Torah is extra harsh with him, so we cannot learn lashes for every speech-only sin from him.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about X? It is special because...": the standard way to attack a comparison
He gets lashes
He pays money

phrases.english: What about the defamer?
He is special, since he is flogged and also pays!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, שֶׁכֵּן לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's derivation from מוציא שם רע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A stricter case (lashes plus payment) cannot teach a rule for milder cases.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: learned from plotting witnesses
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש offers a new source: עדים זוממין get lashes even though their sin is only speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said: He learns it from plotting witnesses. Just as plotting witnesses break a prohibition with no action and are flogged, so too anyone who breaks a prohibition with no action is flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: After עולא's source was rejected, the גמרא offers a new source for רבי יהודה: the case of עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין sin only by testifying falsely, which is speech and not an action. They still get lashes in some cases. ריש לקיש makes this case the model instead of מוציא שם רע.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous idea and brings a new one
Plotting witnesses, caught in false testimony by other witnesses

phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said:
He derives it from plotting witnesses.
Just as plotting witnesses

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: is a prohibition with no action, and one is flogged for it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: so too, for any prohibition with no action, one is flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גָּמַר מֵעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces עולא's rejected source with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns it from עדים זוממין, a speech-only sin that brings lashes.

steps.title: Plotting witnesses need no warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this source too: עדים זוממין are special because they are punished without התראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about plotting witnesses? They are special, because they do not need a warning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's source by pointing out a unique feature of עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally nobody gets lashes unless he was warned (התראה) before sinning. עדים זוממין are punished even without a warning, which makes them a stricter, unusual case. So a rule for normal prohibitions cannot be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before the sin, normally needed for court punishment
They do not need

phrases.english: What about plotting witnesses?
They are special, since they do not need a warning!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין צְרִיכִין הַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's derivation from עדים זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case punished even without התראה is unusually strict, so it cannot teach a general rule.

steps.title: Combining both cases: the common factor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a הצד השוה: each case's special feature is missing in the other, but both share a speech-only sin that brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The defamer will prove it. And the argument goes back to the start: this case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is a prohibition with no action that brings lashes. So too, any prohibition with no action brings lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the derivation by learning from both cases together, using what they have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against "no warning needed": מוציא שם רע does need a warning and still gets lashes, so that is not the reason. Against "flogged and pays": עדים זוממין do not always get both. Since each case's special feature is missing in the other, the only reason left for lashes is what they share: a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: this case shows the objection is not the real reason
And the argument goes back to the start
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
The common factor shared by both cases

steps.confusionAlert: Each case on its own fails. The proof only works when you put both together and look at what they share.

phrases.english: The defamer will prove it.
phrases.notes: The defamer needs a warning and still gets lashes, so "no warning" can't be the real reason.

phrases.english: And the argument goes back to the start:
this case is not like that one,
and that one is not like this one.
The common factor between them:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה וְלוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: a prohibition with no action, and one is flogged for it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: So too, for any prohibition with no action, one is flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע יוֹכִיחַ. וְחָזַר הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attacks of steps 9 and 11 by combining both sources.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הצד השוה: combining two sources so that each one's special feature is cancelled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each source is too special on its own, so the rule has no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together, the only shared reason left for lashes is the speech-only sin itself.

steps.title: Both cases involve a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the common factor: in both cases the payment is a קנס, a feature they share.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about their common factor? Both are special, because both are a fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the הצד השוה by finding something else both cases share that could explain the lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה fails if both cases share some extra strict feature. Here, the payment of מוציא שם רע is a קנס (step 3), and so is the payment of עדים זוממין according to רבי עקיבא (step 4). So maybe the lashes come only in fine-type cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine: a set penalty, not payment for actual damage
That is in them, shared by both

phrases.english: What about the common factor between them?
They are special, since they are a fine!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הצד השוה built in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה from מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases share a קנס, a special strict feature, so the common factor may not apply to ordinary prohibitions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not call it a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רבי יהודה does not agree with רבי עקיבא that the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס, so the cases do not share a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge and saves the derivation for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "both are a fine" attack depends on רבי עקיבא's view that the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס. רבי יהודה disagrees, so to him only מוציא שם רע pays a fine. With no shared fine, the הצד השוה stands, and רבי יהודה has his source.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
Does not hold like (that opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: In step 4 the comparison worked because רבי מאיר agreed with רבי עקיבא. Here it works for the opposite reason: רבי יהודה does not agree with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: Meaning: he does not agree that the payment of plotting witnesses is a fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack of step 13, completing רבי יהודה's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opinion-based: the attack depends on a view רבי יהודה does not hold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve a קנס, so the common factor fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: To רבי יהודה, עדים זוממין do not pay a קנס, so the הצד השוה holds.

steps.title: Both cases have something strict about them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new attack on the הצד השוה: מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין are both strict cases, so they cannot teach about lighter sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can attack it this way: what about the common factor of these two cases? Both of them have a strict side.
steps.whatsHappening: The קנס attack did not work, so the גמרא tries a different attack on the הצד השוה. It says both source cases share a 'strict side', so maybe that is the real reason they get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the גמרא said each case had its own special feature, so neither one could be pushed aside alone. Now the גמרא says: the two features are different, but each one is a kind of strictness. מוציא שם רע gets lashes and also pays, and עדים זוממין are punished without התראה. So maybe only strict cases get lashes for a sin of speech alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The common factor; learning a law from what two cases share
A strict side; something that makes a case more severe
'What about...?' The usual way to point out that a source case is special and cannot teach the new case

steps.confusionAlert: The two 'strict sides' are not the same thing. Each case is strict in its own way. The attack is that being strict in some way is itself the shared feature.

phrases.english: Rather: what about the common factor between them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two source cases, מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין.

phrases.english: since they both have a strict side!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן צַד חָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קנס attack in step 13 was answered in step 14, the גמרא offers a different attack on the same הצד השוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה from מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין that is used as רבי יהודה's source for lashes on a sin of speech alone (step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both source cases are strict in some way, and that shared strictness may be the real reason for the lashes. If so, the rule cannot be carried over to an ordinary sin of speech.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not accept the 'strict side' attack
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה does not knock down a הצד השוה just because each case has some strict side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He does not use 'a strict side' to knock down a הצד השוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה. It says he simply does not accept this kind of attack against a הצד השוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, two different strict features do not add up to one shared feature. Only a real feature found in both cases, like a קנס, could break the הצד השוה. So the source for lashes on a sin of speech alone stays in place for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He attacks or knocks down an argument

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the הצד השוה from מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין holds up. Both attacks fail: the קנס attack and the 'strict side' attack.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה?
He does not attack using 'a strict side'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? צַד חָמוּר לָא פָּרֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack of step 15 and closes the discussion of רבי יהודה's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The opinion holder does not accept this method of attack
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the shared 'strict side' breaks the הצד השוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does not accept 'a strict side' as a reason to break a הצד השוה, so his source stands.

steps.title: What do רבנן learn from 'You shall not bear false witness'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן and asks what רבנן use the verse לא תענה for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן, what do they learn from this verse, 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier argument on the דף. It asks what רבנן do with the פסוק לא תענה ברעך עד שקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said עדים זוממין who tried to get someone lashes receive two sets of lashes: one for breaking לא תענה and one from ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם. רבנן said they get only one set. So the גמרא asks: if רבנן give no lashes for breaking לא תענה, what is that verse for?

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor', one of the עשרת הדברות
What do they learn from it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר״
phrases.english: And רבנן, this verse, 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor',
what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי יהודה and goes back to the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן about the lashes of עדים זוממין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבנן use the verse לא תענה for, since they do not give lashes for breaking it.

steps.title: For רבנן, the verse is the warning for עדים זוממין
steps.stepSummary: רבנן need לא תענה as the warning (אזהרה) for the punishment of עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that verse as the warning for עדים זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבנן, לא תענה is the warning that comes with the punishment of עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not punish without first warning, so every punishment needs a verse that forbids the act. For רבנן, לא תענה is that warning, and the punishment comes from ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם. So the verse is used, but it does not bring a second set of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning; the verse that forbids an act, which a Torah punishment needs
He needs it for something else
False witnesses shown to be lying because they were somewhere else at the time

phrases.english: That verse is needed
as a warning for עדים זוממין.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְאַזְהָרָה לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבנן, לא תענה is the אזהרה for the punishment of עדים זוממין, not a source for extra lashes.

steps.title: Where does רבי מאיר find the warning?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי מאיר uses לא תענה for its own set of lashes, the גמרא asks where he finds the warning for עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, where does he get the warning for עדים זוממין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the same question on רבי מאיר. He uses לא תענה for extra lashes, so where is his warning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives a full set of lashes just for breaking לא תענה. That verse is then a law of its own, and it is not the warning for the punishment of ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם. So the second punishment still needs a warning from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַזְהָרָה לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And רבי מאיר, from where does he get a warning for עדים זוממין?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַזְהָרָה לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 18 gave רבנן's answer. Now the גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which verse is the warning for עדים זוממין according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns the warning from 'and those who remain shall hear'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says רבי מאיר learns the warning from 'והנשארים ישמעו ויראו ולא יוסיפו עוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: he learns it from 'And those who remain shall hear and fear, and shall not do any more...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives רבי מאיר a different verse for the warning. It comes from the section about עדים זוממין itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולא יוסיפו עוד', 'they shall not do any more', are read as a ban on acting as עדים זוממין. That gives רבי מאיר a warning for the punishment of ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם. It leaves לא תענה free to bring its own lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from (a verse)
'And they shall not do any more'; read here as a ban, a warning

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said:
He learns it from: 'And those who remain shall hear and fear,
phrases.notes: דברים 19:20, right after the punishment of עדים זוממין.

phrases.english: and shall not do any more.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִוְּהַנִּשְׁאָרִים יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ וְלֹא יֹסִיפוּ עוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר takes the warning for עדים זוממין from 'והנשארים ישמעו ויראו ולא יוסיפו עוד'.

steps.title: What do רבנן do with that verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבנן learn from 'והנשארים ישמעו ויראו', since they took the warning from לא תענה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? What do they use that verse for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבנן. They already have their warning from לא תענה, so it asks what they do with the verse 'והנשארים ישמעו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has to account for both verses. רבנן used לא תענה as the warning, so 'והנשארים ישמעו' seems to have no job for them. The גמרא asks what that job is.

phrases.english: And רבנן?
phrases.notes: This is short for: what do רבנן learn from the verse 'והנשארים ישמעו'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי מאיר a use for 'והנשארים ישמעו', the גמרא asks what רבנן use it for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבנן learn from the verse 'והנשארים ישמעו ויראו'.

steps.title: רבנן need that verse for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: רבנן need 'והנשארים ישמעו' for a different teaching. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer that רבנן use 'והנשארים ישמעו' for a different purpose. This line only opens the answer, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מיבעי ליה tells us רבנן do not ignore the verse. They need it for some other law. The next lines will say what that law is.

phrases.english: That verse is needed for them

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 21. The answer is completed in the following text.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use 'והנשארים ישמעו' for another teaching, which is spelled out in the continuation.
